1.overview: At the LORD’s command in the Wilderness of Sinai, Moses and Aaron count Israel’s men aged twenty and older who can serve in the army, with twelve tribal leaders assisting; the total is 603,550. The Levites are excluded from the census and assigned to carry, maintain, and guard the tabernacle, while the other Israelites camp by their divisions, and the people carry out the LORD’s commands.

2.overview: The LORD instructs Moses and Aaron to arrange Israel’s tribes around the Tent of Meeting under four standards, with Judah’s camp to the east, Reuben’s to the south, Ephraim’s to the west, and Dan’s to the north. The chapter gives each camp’s tribal leaders and numbers, sets their order of travel with the Levites and Tent of Meeting in the center, and reports that the Israelites follow the arrangement while the Levites remain uncounted among them.

sections.heading: Dan’s camp on the north and Israel’s order

3.overview: The chapter names Aaron’s sons and assigns the Levites to assist the priests, replacing Israel’s firstborn because the firstborn belong to the LORD. Moses counts the Levite clans and their tabernacle duties, then counts Israel’s firstborn and collects redemption money for the 273 who exceed the Levites.

sections.heading: Aaron’s Sons and the Levites’ Appointment

4.overview: The LORD directs Moses and Aaron to count the Kohathites, Gershonites, and Merarites aged thirty to fifty who serve at the Tent of Meeting, and assigns each clan its transport duties under priestly oversight. Moses, Aaron, and Israel’s leaders count 8,580 Levites and assign each man his work and burden as the LORD commands.

sections.heading: Census and Assignment of the Levites

5.overview: The LORD commands Israel to remove people with specified impurities from the camp and sets rules for confession, restitution, and sacred gifts. He establishes a priestly procedure for a husband’s suspicion of his wife’s adultery, including an oath and bitter water whose effects distinguish guilt from innocence.

sections.heading: The Bitter Water and Its Outcomes

6.overview: The LORD gives Moses the regulations for a Nazirite vow, including its restrictions, cleansing after accidental defilement, and offerings and rites at the vow’s completion. He then instructs Moses to have Aaron and his sons bless Israel, promising to place his name on the people and bless them.

sections.heading: Defilement and Completion of the Vow

7.overview: After the tabernacle and altar are consecrated, Israel’s leaders provide six carts and twelve oxen for the Levites’ work, with none assigned to the Kohathites. Over twelve days, each tribal leader presents an identical dedication offering for the altar, whose offerings are totaled, and Moses hears the LORD’s voice from above the ark’s mercy seat.

sections.heading: Offering Totals and the LORD’s Voice

8.overview: The LORD directs Aaron to arrange the lampstand’s seven lamps, then instructs Moses on cleansing and presenting the Levites for service in place of Israel’s firstborn. Moses, Aaron, and Israel carry out the instructions, and the LORD sets the Levites’ service ages and retirement duties.

sections.heading: Cleansing and Presentation of the Levites

9.overview: In the Wilderness of Sinai, the Israelites observe Passover at the appointed time, and the LORD provides a second-month observance for those unclean from a dead body or away on a journey, while requiring the same statutes for foreigners and native Israelites. The cloud covers the tabernacle and appears like fire at night, directing when Israel camps and sets out at the LORD’s command through Moses.

10.overview: The LORD instructs Moses to make silver trumpets for assembling Israel, signaling the camps to march, and marking battles and occasions of worship. As the cloud lifts, Israel follows its ordered divisions from Sinai toward Paran; Moses invites Hobab to join them, and he speaks when the ark sets out and comes to rest.

11.overview: After the people complain about hardship and crave meat, the LORD sends fire and later promises meat, while Moses protests the burden of leading Israel. The LORD appoints seventy elders to share Moses’ burden, gives them the Spirit, sends quail, and strikes the people with a plague at Kibroth-hattaavah before Israel moves to Hazeroth.

sections.heading: The people crave meat and Moses protests

12.overview: Miriam and Aaron criticize Moses over his Cushite wife and question whether the LORD speaks only through him. The LORD affirms Moses’ unique role, afflicts Miriam with leprosy, orders her confinement for seven days, and the people then travel from Hazeroth to the Wilderness of Paran.

13.overview: The LORD commands Moses to send twelve tribal leaders from Kadesh to scout Canaan, and Moses gives Hoshea the name Joshua. After forty days, the scouts return with fruit and report that the land is fertile but its fortified cities and powerful inhabitants make conquest seem impossible, while Caleb urges the people to take possession of it.

sections.heading: The Scouts Report on the Land
Caleb’s Challenge and the Bad Report

14.overview: The Israelites reject Joshua and Caleb’s report, grumble against Moses and Aaron, and threaten to stone the two spies, prompting the LORD to announce judgment. Moses intercedes, and the LORD pardons the people but decrees that the adult generation will die in the wilderness while Caleb, Joshua, and the children will enter the land; after the scouts are struck by a plague, the Israelites attempt to advance without the LORD and are routed at Hormah.

sections.heading: The people reject Joshua and Caleb
Moses intercedes and the LORD responds
The wilderness judgment and the scouts’ fate
The failed advance into the hill country

15.overview: The LORD gives Moses regulations for grain and drink offerings in the land, including equal requirements for native Israelites and resident foreigners, and instructions for offerings when the community or an individual sins unintentionally. He distinguishes defiant sin, commands the execution of a man who gathers wood on the Sabbath, and orders Israel to wear tassels as reminders of his commandments.

16.overview: Korah, Dathan, Abiram, and 250 leaders challenge Moses and Aaron’s authority, and Moses proposes a test before the LORD while Dathan and Abiram refuse his summons. The earth swallows the rebels, fire consumes the incense offerers, their censers become an altar covering, and Aaron’s incense halts a plague after 14,700 people die.

sections.heading: Korah’s Challenge to Moses and Aaron
Dathan and Abiram Refuse; Judgment Falls

17.overview: The LORD tells Moses to collect twelve tribal staffs and place them before the Testimony, declaring that the chosen man’s staff will sprout. Aaron’s staff sprouts and bears almonds, the LORD commands it to be kept as a sign against grumbling, and the Israelites fear that anyone approaching the tabernacle will die.

18.overview: The LORD assigns Aaron and his sons responsibility for the priesthood and sanctuary, with the Levites assisting in the Tent of Meeting under defined limits. He gives Aaron’s household portions of Israel’s offerings, assigns the Levites Israel’s tithes instead of land inheritance, and requires them to offer a tenth of those tithes to the LORD for Aaron.

19.overview: The LORD instructs Moses and Aaron on preparing and keeping the ashes of an unblemished red heifer as water for purification, including the duties and temporary uncleanness of those involved. The chapter sets out how people and objects made unclean by contact with a corpse are purified on the third and seventh days, and the consequences of failing to be purified.

sections.heading: The Red Heifer and Its Ashes
Uncleanness from Contact with the Dead

20.overview: At Kadesh, Miriam dies, and Israel complains over the lack of water; Moses strikes the rock, water flows, and the LORD says Moses and Aaron will not lead Israel into the land. Edom refuses Israel passage through its territory, and at Mount Hor Aaron transfers his priestly garments to Eleazar, dies, and is mourned by Israel for thirty days.

sections.heading: Water from the Rock at Meribah

21.overview: Israel defeats the Canaanite king of Arad, then complains during the journey from Mount Hor and survives the venomous snakes by looking at Moses’ bronze serpent; the Israelites travel through the wilderness and sing at the well God provides. Israel defeats Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan, takes their territories, and occupies the land from the Arnon to Bashan.

22.overview: Balak, king of Moab, summons Balaam to curse Israel, but God first forbids him and then permits him to go only with strict instructions. On the journey the angel of the LORD confronts Balaam, who reaches Moab and tells Balak he can speak only what God puts in his mouth.

23.overview: At Balak’s direction, Balaam offers sacrifices and delivers an oracle declaring that he cannot curse Israel, whom God has not cursed. After a second set of sacrifices, Balaam proclaims God’s unchangeable blessing and Israel’s strength, while Balak takes him to Peor for another attempt.

24.overview: Balaam sees Israel encamped and, moved by the Spirit of God, blesses Israel in an oracle describing its prosperity and strength; Balak angrily dismisses him, and Balaam insists that he can speak only what the LORD commands. Balaam then foretells a ruler from Israel who will strike Moab and Edom, pronounces further oracles against Amalek, the Kenites, Asshur, and Eber, and returns home as Balak departs.

25.overview: At Shittim, Israel joins Moabite worship of Baal of Peor, and the LORD commands judgment as a plague strikes the people. Phinehas kills Zimri and Cozbi, halting the plague, and the LORD grants him a covenant of peace and permanent priesthood while commanding Israel to attack Midian.

sections.heading: The Victims Named and Midian Targeted

26.overview: After the plague, the LORD directs Moses and Eleazar to count Israel’s military-age men by tribe on the plains of Moab, recording 601,730 and noting the clans of the Levites separately. The LORD assigns tribal inheritances according to population and by lot, while the chapter states that none counted in the earlier wilderness census remains except Caleb and Joshua.

27.overview: The daughters of Zelophehad ask for an inheritance, and the LORD rules that they may inherit and establishes an order of succession for cases without sons. The LORD tells Moses he will die before entering the land, and Moses commissions Joshua as Israel’s leader.

sections.heading: Moses’s Death and Request for a Successor

28.overview: The LORD prescribes daily, Sabbath, and monthly burnt offerings, including their grain and drink offerings and a goat for the monthly sin offering. He also specifies the offerings and sacred assemblies for Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread and for the Feast of Weeks and its firstfruits.

29.overview: The LORD prescribes offerings for the seventh month: the trumpet day on the first, the day of atonement on the tenth, and the seven-day Feast of Tabernacles beginning on the fifteenth, with the number of bulls decreasing each day. He sets out the offerings for the solemn assembly on the eighth day, and Moses conveys all the instructions to Israel.

sections.heading: Offerings for the Day of Atonement
Offerings for the Feast of Tabernacles

30.overview: Moses gives Israel’s tribal heads rules requiring a man to fulfill his vows and describing when a father or husband may nullify a woman’s vow. Vows made by widows and divorced women remain binding, while a husband’s silence confirms his wife’s vow and delayed nullification makes him bear her iniquity.

sections.heading: Vows of Widows and Married Women

31.overview: At the LORD’s command, Israel’s forces led by Phinehas defeat Midian, kill its kings and Balaam, and bring captives and plunder to the camp in Moab. Moses orders the captives and goods purified and apportioned, with tributes for Eleazar and the Levites, and receives the officers’ gold offering for the Tent of Meeting.

sections.heading: Division of the Captives and Plunder

32.overview: The Reubenites and Gadites ask Moses, Eleazar, and Israel’s leaders to possess the livestock-suitable land east of the Jordan, and Moses warns that their withdrawal could discourage Israel as their fathers did. They pledge to fight alongside the other tribes before settling their families east of the Jordan; Moses assigns land to Reuben, Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh, and the tribes build cities and capture territory in Gilead and Bashan.

33.overview: Moses records Israel’s journey from Rameses through successive wilderness camps to the plains of Moab, including Aaron’s death on Mount Hor. There the LORD commands Israel to drive out Canaan’s inhabitants, destroy their idols, take and divide the land, and warns of the consequences if they leave the inhabitants in place.

sections.heading: Aaron’s Death and Arrival in Moab

34.overview: The LORD defines Canaan’s southern, western, northern, and eastern boundaries as the inheritance of Israel’s nine and a half tribes, noting that Reuben, Gad, and half-Manasseh already receive land east of the Jordan. The LORD names Eleazar, Joshua, and one leader from each tribe to apportion the inheritance.

35.overview: The LORD commands Israel to give the Levites forty-eight cities with pasturelands, including six cities of refuge. He establishes rules distinguishing murder from accidental killing, governing refuge and judgment, and forbidding ransom for murderers or premature release from refuge, because bloodshed pollutes the land where the LORD dwells.

36.overview: The clan heads of Gilead raise the concern that Zelophehad’s daughters’ inheritance could pass to another tribe if they marry outside their father’s tribe. Moses rules that women who inherit land must marry within their father’s tribe, and Zelophehad’s daughters marry within Manasseh so their inheritance remains there; the chapter closes with a notice of the commandments given on the plains of Moab.

sections.heading: Moses’ Ruling on Marriage and Inheritance
